Token totals are null unless the provider reports usage for every attempted call.
No fixed generation seed; temperature 0.2; latency includes model calls and local validation.

content.adaptation_note: As a beginner, focus on mastering form before increasing weight or intensity. If a session feels too easy, increase the number of reps or reduce rest time slightly. If it feels too hard, reduce the number of sets or reps. Listen to your body and prioritize consistent movement over pushing to failure.
content.safety_note: Always perform a 5-minute warm-up before starting your workout. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain or dizziness. Ensure your equipment is stable and your space is clear of obstacles. Consult a healthcare provider before starting a new exercise program if you have any pre-existing conditions.

workouts.focus: Active recovery and full body flow

content.adaptation_note: As a beginner, focus on mastering form before increasing weight or volume. If a session feels too easy, add one set to the main compound movements. If it feels too hard, reduce the number of sets by one. Ensure you are drinking enough water throughout the day to support energy levels.
content.safety_note: Always listen to your body. Stop any exercise if you feel sharp pain. Keep your back neutral during squats and bridges. Ensure the surface for incline push-ups is stable and non-slip.

content.adaptation_note: As a beginner, focus on mastering form before increasing weight or intensity. If 10 reps feel too easy, slow down the tempo or add light dumbbells to squats and curls. If they feel too hard, reduce reps to 8 or perform the movement without weights. Ensure you are drinking enough water throughout the day to support energy levels.
content.safety_note: Always listen to your body. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain (not to be confused with muscle burn). Ensure your incline push-up surface is stable and non-slip. Keep your core engaged during dead bugs to protect your lower back.
